subproblem.title: Bounded open Lipschitz piece carrying the part of a C¹ antilipschitz chart over a compact set
subproblem.statement: Let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q be C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ), let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, let c > 0 satisfy c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω, and let K ⊆ ℝ^Q be compact (ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with the Euclidean norm). Then there exist an open set s ⊆ ℝⁿ and a constant L ∈ ℝ≥0 such that s ⊆ Ω, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s, s is bounded, and Φ is L-Lipschitz on s.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (K : Set (Eucl Q)), IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → IsCompact K → ∃ (s : Set (Eucl n)) (L : ℝ≥0), IsOpen s ∧ s ⊆ Ω ∧ Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' K ⊆ s ∧ Bornology.IsBounded s ∧ LipschitzOnWith L Φ s
subproblem.natural_proof:
Setting and notation.
- Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q is C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ is open, c > 0 satisfies c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω, and K ⊆ ℝ^Q is compact.
- ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with the Euclidean norm |·|; B_r(x) is the open ball and B̄_r(x) the closed ball.
- This is steps 2–3 of the parent proof: the choice of the bounded open set s = Ω ∩ B_ρ(w₀) and the Lipschitz bound on it, applied there with K = tsupport h.

1. (Empty case.) Suppose Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = ∅. Take s := ∅ and L := 0. Then:
   - s is open, s ⊆ Ω, and s is bounded;
   - Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = ∅ ⊆ s;
   - every map is 0-Lipschitz on ∅ (Mathlib `lipschitzOnWith_empty`).
   This proves the claim in this case. From now on assume Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ≠ ∅.

2. (Choice of the ball.) Fix w₀ ∈ Ω with Φ(w₀) ∈ K. K is compact, hence bounded, so there is D ∈ ℝ with |y − y′| ≤ D for all y, y′ ∈ K (`Metric.isBounded_iff`). Put ρ := D/c + 1 and s := Ω ∩ B_ρ(w₀).

3. (s is open, contained in Ω, and bounded.) s is the intersection of the open sets Ω and B_ρ(w₀), so s is open. Clearly s ⊆ Ω. Also s ⊆ B_ρ(w₀), a bounded set, so s is bounded.

4. (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s.) Let v ∈ Ω with Φ(v) ∈ K.
   - Apply the lower bound to w = v, w′ = w₀ (both in Ω), then the choice of D (Φ(v), Φ(w₀) ∈ K): c|v − w₀| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(w₀)| ≤ D.
   - Dividing by c > 0 gives |v − w₀| ≤ D/c < D/c + 1 = ρ, so v ∈ B_ρ(w₀).
   - Together with v ∈ Ω this gives v ∈ s.

5. (Bound on the derivative.) Since Φ is C¹, the map x ↦ DΦ(x) = fderiv ℝ Φ x is continuous (`ContDiff.continuous_fderiv`, using 1 ≤ 1). The closed ball B̄ := B̄_ρ(w₀) is compact (finite dimension). So there is C ∈ ℝ with ‖DΦ(x)‖ ≤ C for all x ∈ B̄ (`IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn`). Put L := max(C, 0) = Real.toNNReal C ∈ ℝ≥0. Then ‖DΦ(x)‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ B̄.

6. (Mean value inequality.) Φ is differentiable at every point (C¹, 1 ≠ 0) and B̄ is convex. The mean value inequality on convex sets (`Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le`, with ‖DΦ(x)‖₊ ≤ L on B̄) gives |Φ(x) − Φ(x′)| ≤ L|x − x′| for all x, x′ ∈ B̄. That is, Φ is L-Lipschitz on B̄.

7. (Restriction to s.) s ⊆ B_ρ(w₀) ⊆ B̄, so Φ is L-Lipschitz on s (`LipschitzOnWith.mono`).

8. (Conclusion.) By steps 3, 4 and 7, the set s and the constant L satisfy all the requirements: s is open, s ⊆ Ω, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s, s is bounded, and Φ is L-Lipschitz on s. ∎

Lean note: every lemma used is in the frozen scope `import GMT.Ch06.Submission`. The proof is a single theorem with no imports and no helpers.
proof_key_steps: If Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = ∅, take s = ∅ and L = 0 (lipschitzOnWith_empty).
Otherwise pick w₀ ∈ Ω with Φ(w₀) ∈ K and a distance bound D for K; set ρ = D/c + 1 and s = Ω ∩ B_ρ(w₀). Then s is open, s ⊆ Ω, and s is bounded.
Antilipschitz bound: c|v − w₀| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(w₀)| ≤ D gives |v − w₀| < ρ, hence Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s.
DΦ is continuous, so ‖DΦ‖ ≤ C on the compact convex ball B̄_ρ(w₀). The mean value inequality makes Φ (Real.toNNReal C)-Lipschitz on B̄_ρ(w₀) ⊇ s.

subproblem.title: From the nonnegative area identity on a bounded piece to the signed area formula for compactly supported continuous functions
subproblem.statement: Let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q be continuous, let Ω, s ⊆ ℝⁿ be open with s ⊆ Ω and s bounded, and assume Φ is injective on Ω. Let J : ℝⁿ → ℝ be continuous with J ≥ 0, and let h : ℝ^Q → ℝ be continuous with compact support such that Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(tsupport h) ⊆ s. Suppose that for every Borel g : ℝ^Q → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_{Φ(s)} g dHⁿ = ∫⁻_s ofReal(J(v))·g(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v). Then ∫_{Φ(Ω)} h dHⁿ = ∫_Ω J(v)h(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v). Here Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q, Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, ∫ is the Bochner set integral and ∫⁻ the lintegral.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl Q) (Ω s : Set (Eucl n)) (J : Eucl n → ℝ) (h : Eucl Q → ℝ), IsOpen Ω → IsOpen s → s ⊆ Ω → Bornology.IsBounded s → Continuous Φ → InjOn Φ Ω → Continuous J → (∀ v, 0 ≤ J v) → Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' tsupport h ⊆ s → (∀ g : Eucl Q → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → ∫⁻ y in Φ '' s, g y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) = ∫⁻ v in s, ENNReal.ofReal (J v) * g (Φ v) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n))) → ∫ x in Φ '' Ω, h x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) = ∫ v in Ω, J v * h (Φ v) ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Setting and notation.
- Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q is continuous; Ω, s ⊆ ℝⁿ are open with s ⊆ Ω and s bounded; Φ is injective on Ω.
- J : ℝⁿ → ℝ is continuous with J ≥ 0.
- h : ℝ^Q → ℝ is continuous with compact support; K := tsupport h; Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s.
- (H): for every Borel g : ℝ^Q → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_{Φ(s)} g dHⁿ = ∫⁻_s ofReal(J(v))·g(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v).
- Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q and Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ; ∫ is the Bochner set integral, ∫⁻ the lintegral. Write F(v) := J(v)·h(Φ(v)).
- This is steps 5–6 of the parent proof, together with the Borel measurability of Φ(Ω) from step 2(b). (H) is the identity the parent obtains in step 4, with J = JΦ.
- Hⁿ(Φ(s)) < ∞ is obtained from (H) with g ≡ 1 instead of the Lipschitz image bound of parent step 3. This is the same finiteness the parent uses in step 5.

1. (Vanishing off K.) If y ∉ K, then h(y) = 0 (`image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport`).

2. (Bounds.)
   (a) s is bounded in the proper space ℝⁿ, so its closure is compact (`Bornology.IsBounded.isCompact_closure`). J is continuous, so there is J_max with |J(v)| ≤ J_max on the closure of s (`IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn`). Since J ≥ 0, we get 0 ≤ J(v) ≤ J_max for every v ∈ s.
   (b) h is continuous with compact support, so there is M with |h(y)| ≤ M for all y (`Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support`).
   (c) Lⁿ(s) < ∞, because s is bounded and Lⁿ is finite on compact sets (`Bornology.IsBounded.measure_lt_top`).

3. (Hⁿ(Φ(s)) < ∞.) Apply (H) to the measurable function g ≡ 1. Then Hⁿ(Φ(s)) = ∫⁻_{Φ(s)} 1 dHⁿ = ∫⁻_s ofReal(J(v))·1 dLⁿ. Since ofReal is monotone and J ≤ J_max on s, this is ≤ ∫⁻_s ofReal(J_max) dLⁿ = ofReal(J_max)·Lⁿ(s), which is < ∞ by 2(c).

4. (Integrability.)
   - h is continuous (hence strongly measurable), |h| ≤ M, and Hⁿ(Φ(s)) < ∞ by step 3. So h is Hⁿ-integrable on Φ(s) (`Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded`).
   - F is continuous, since J, h and Φ are, hence strongly measurable. For v ∈ s, |F(v)| = J(v)|h(Φ(v))| ≤ J_max·M by 2(a) and 2(b). Since Lⁿ(s) < ∞, F is Lⁿ-integrable on s.

5. (The two nonnegative identities.) The functions g₊ := ofReal ∘ h and g₋ := ofReal ∘ (−h) are Borel, because h is continuous and ofReal is measurable. By (H):
   ∫⁻_{Φ(s)} ofReal(h) dHⁿ = ∫⁻_s ofReal(J(v))·ofReal(h(Φ(v))) dLⁿ, and
   ∫⁻_{Φ(s)} ofReal(−h) dHⁿ = ∫⁻_s ofReal(J(v))·ofReal(−h(Φ(v))) dLⁿ.
   Since J(v) ≥ 0 and ofReal(a)·ofReal(b) = ofReal(ab) for a ≥ 0 (`ENNReal.ofReal_mul`), the right-hand integrands are ofReal(F(v)) and ofReal(J(v)·(−h(Φ(v)))) = ofReal(−F(v)).

6. (Signed identity on s.) For an integrable real function f, ∫ f = toReal(∫⁻ ofReal(f)) − toReal(∫⁻ ofReal(−f)) (`integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part`). Apply this to h on (Φ(s), Hⁿ) and to F on (s, Lⁿ); both are integrable by step 4. Substituting the two identities of step 5 gives
   ∫_{Φ(s)} h dHⁿ = toReal(∫⁻_s ofReal(F) dLⁿ) − toReal(∫⁻_s ofReal(−F) dLⁿ) = ∫_s F dLⁿ.

7. (Measurability of Φ(Ω).) Ω is open, hence Borel. Φ is continuous on Ω and injective on Ω, and ℝⁿ is Polish. By the Lusin–Souslin theorem (`MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn`), Φ(Ω) is Borel.

8. (Extension on the source.) Let v ∈ Ω ∖ s. Then Φ(v) ∉ K, since otherwise v ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) ⊆ s. By step 1, h(Φ(v)) = 0, so F(v) = 0. Since s ⊆ Ω and Ω is measurable, ∫_Ω F dLⁿ = ∫_s F dLⁿ (`setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero`).

9. (Extension on the target.) Let y ∈ Φ(Ω) ∖ Φ(s) and write y = Φ(v) with v ∈ Ω. Then v ∉ s (otherwise y ∈ Φ(s)), so Φ(v) ∉ K as in step 8, and h(y) = 0. Since Φ(s) ⊆ Φ(Ω) and Φ(Ω) is measurable by step 7, the same lemma gives ∫_{Φ(Ω)} h dHⁿ = ∫_{Φ(s)} h dHⁿ.

10. (Conclusion.) By steps 9, 6 and 8: ∫_{Φ(Ω)} h dHⁿ = ∫_{Φ(s)} h dHⁿ = ∫_s F dLⁿ = ∫_Ω J(v)h(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v). ∎

Lean note: every lemma used is in the frozen scope `import GMT.Ch06.Submission`. The proof is a single theorem with no imports and no helpers.
proof_key_steps: h vanishes off K = tsupport h. Bounds: 0 ≤ J ≤ J_max on s (compact closure), |h| ≤ M, Lⁿ(s) < ∞ (s bounded).
(H) with g ≡ 1 gives Hⁿ(Φ(s)) ≤ ofReal(J_max)·Lⁿ(s) < ∞. Hence h is integrable on (Φ(s), Hⁿ) and J·(h∘Φ) is integrable on (s, Lⁿ).

(H) with g = ofReal∘h and g = ofReal∘(−h), together with J ≥ 0 and ENNReal.ofReal_mul, gives the positive- and negative-part identities. integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part then yields ∫_{Φ(s)} h dHⁿ = ∫_s J·(h∘Φ) dLⁿ.
Φ(Ω) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin). The integrands vanish on Ω∖s and on Φ(Ω)∖Φ(s), so setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero extends the identity to Ω and Φ(Ω).

Applying it to ofReal(h) and ofReal(−h), using J ≥ 0, proves the signed identity. Lusin–Souslin and support containment justify extension to Ω and Φ(Ω). The parent independently supplies the assumed nonnegative identity from the pinned weighted area formula, so there is no circularity or missing child dependency.
